claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I need to gather some information about your circumstances. Let me start with a few questions.

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me how many children you have and their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 13 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. 

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

**Are you responsible for Alex?** By this I mean, does Alex live with you, or do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do contribute towards their upkeep. I help out with money for their needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**Can you tell me approximately how much you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week?** I need to know this because to be eligible, you would need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit rate, which is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £26 a week towards Alex's needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Does Alex live with someone else who might also be claiming Child Benefit for them?** For example, does Alex live with their other parent or another guardian?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with their other parent, but they're not claiming Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Now I need to ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not living in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

**Which country are you currently living in?** This is important because there are specific rules about claiming Child Benefit when you're living abroad, and eligibility can depend on which country you're in and your circumstances there.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently living in Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Can you tell me about your work situation in Spain? Are you employed there, self-employed, or in any other type of work arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm working in Spain, yes. I have a job here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**Are you employed by a UK employer or a Spanish employer?** And also, **are you or have you been paying UK National Insurance contributions while working in Spain?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm employed by a Spanish employer and I'm not paying UK National Insurance contributions.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

Just a couple more questions:

**Are you a UK national, or do you hold citizenship of another country?** And **does Alex live in the UK or abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a UK national. Alex lives in the UK with their other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information.

One final question to complete my assessment:

**When did you move to Spain to live and work there?** Specifically, I need to know if this move happened before or after 1 January 2021 (when the Brexit transition period ended).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I moved to Spain about two years ago, so that would be after 2021.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete

Thank you for providing all the information I needed. Based on your circumstances, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

While Alex meets the age requirements (being 13 years old) and you do contribute enough towards their upkeep (£26 per week, which exceeds the minimum Child Benefit rate), the issue is with your residency and work situation.

Since you moved to Spain after January 2021 (after the Brexit transition period ended), you are working for a Spanish employer, and you are not paying UK National Insurance contributions, you do not meet the requirements to claim Child Benefit from abroad. 

Generally, to claim Child Benefit while living in an EU country after Brexit, you would need to either:
- Be working for a UK employer and paying UK National Insurance, or
- Fall under specific exceptions related to the EU Withdrawal Agreement (which typically applies to those who moved before the transition period ended)

Since neither of these applies to your situation, you are unfortunately not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time.
